P1.claim: In the post-migration cohort, S(90) <= 0.45 and the conditional probability of adjudication in the second year given still unjudged at one year is below 0.20; scorable only if at least 40 remain at risk at day 365.
P1.was_it_at_risk: yes, and it lost by one point on the second half and by seven on the first
P1.what_the_argument_needed: whether Reported is a queue or an absorbing state. It is a queue: the sentence written in advance for this outcome is the one the work publishes.
P1.not_rewritten: F-059 forbids adjusting a prediction once the numbers are in.

P2.claim: In the cohort, the pending share of errata against obsoleted RFCs exceeds that against non-obsoleted RFCs by at least 3 points, n >= 100 in each group.
P2.was_it_at_risk: yes, and deliberately against the age gradient, which the cohort restriction controls
P2.what_the_argument_needed: whether a published rule that pre-decides a class sits unapplied on that class. It does not: the class its rule pre-decides is the class this institution disposes of.

P3.claim: In the cohort, the pending share of errata against RFCs with no working group exceeds that of errata against RFCs with one by at least 3 points, n >= 100 in each group.
P3.what_the_argument_needed: whether the un-normed state concentrates where the addressee is structurally thinner. It does not.

P4.claim: In the cohort, the pending share of Editorial errata is lower than that of Technical by at least 2 points, and the median wait among adjudicated errata is shorter for Editorial than for Technical.
P4.measured: 5.64% (50 of 887) against 30.21% (458 of 1516): 24.57 points; median wait 3 days against 106 days
P4.f070_check: The argument uses both numbers directly: sections 6 and 10 of the work are built on them, and the Kaplan-Meier medians of the two paths (5 days against 389) are the same quantity measured with censoring included. Scored a win, not a miss.
P4.was_it_at_risk: yes: Session 72 had already published that the pending EDITORIAL reports are the older ones, which reads against this prediction until the routing explains both.

P5.claim: In the cohort, zero records have an update_date earlier than their submit_date, and at most ten carry the migration date 2019-09-10.
P5.measured: 0 negatives; 0 migration-stamped; 0 adjudicated records missing an update_date
P5.note: Written to be checked rather than won. Its winning is what makes P1's curve believable; had it lost, the work would have reported no curve. For contrast the same estimate over the whole contaminated record says 85.0% unjudged at 90 days and 75.0% at two years, against the clean cohort's 51.8% and 30.6%.

postscript.what: S58's BLOCKING gate item bit, thirteen days after it was filed, on this session's own follow-up commit.
postscript.how: The follow-up commit changed journal/2026-08-28.md and nothing else. The gate computes the works a branch touched with awk '$1 == "works" && NF > 2', gets an empty list, and runs `tools/validate_v3_night.py <tree> --only` with no names. In the validator, `--only` with nothing after it produces an empty set, and `if only and slug not in only` treats an empty set as 'no scope given' -- so every work in the repository is checked, the three inherited works of early July fail on missing author and medium, and the branch is refused with refused_validation.
postscript.the_fix_this_practice_cannot_land: One line in tools/validate_v3_night.py: `if only is not None and slug not in only`. The file is a protected path in the gate's own PROTECT_RE -- deliberately, since a gate that can rewrite its own check is not a gate -- so this practice can state the fix and cannot make it. That is what S58 meant by BLOCKING and it is now demonstrated rather than predicted.
postscript.what_it_cost: The refusal is recorded here and in the journal, and the follow-up was re-pushed with this file changed so that the branch touches a work directory and the gate has something to scope its check to. Nothing was worked around: the same commit lands by carrying its record into the work it is about, which it should have done in the first place.
postscript.and_a_sentence_of_tonight's_that_is_now_: The journal's opening section says S58's item 'did not bite'. It bit ninety seconds after the journal landed. The sentence stands and is corrected by a dated paragraph, not edited away.
